input.reasoning:
Estimate built bottom-up from 24 backlog items totalling 203 story points. Using a team velocity/complexity approach: converted points to engineering hours using an average of ~7 hours/point for blended full-stack work (typical for small-to-mid teams with design, dev, test, review cycles), then split hours across roles based on task nature (backend-heavy, frontend-heavy, infra, QA, data migration, etc.). Role hours were capped against available FTE capacity over an assumed ~5-month (22-week) delivery window to check feasibility:
- Backend Developer: 1.5 FTE x 22 weeks x 40h = 1320h capacity
- Frontend Developer: 1.0 FTE x 22 weeks x 40h = 880h capacity
- QA Engineer: 0.6 FTE x 22 weeks x 40h = 528h capacity
- DevOps Engineer: 0.4 FTE x 22 weeks x 40h = 352h capacity

Allocated hours were kept within these envelopes, with DevOps and QA being the tightest constraints (thin staffing noted as an assumption/risk). Backend carries the largest share due to RBAC, payments, migration, audit log, multi-currency, and search. Frontend carries dashboard, design system, invoice UI, accessibility, responsive layout. QA is stretched thin given 24 tasks incl. compliance/payment-critical work — flagged as understaffed. DevOps is thin given CI/CD, observability, decommission, and support for migration/payments infra.

Non-labour costs include Stripe integration sandbox/production fees (nominal), staging/cloud infrastructure during build, and a data migration tooling/environment cost for the Oracle extract. A contingency line covers estimation uncertainty since no historical actuals exist for this project.

Total labour computed directly from hours x rates per role. Three scenarios (P50/P70/P90) reflect increasing uncertainty buffers, mainly driven by the high-risk items: legacy data migration (21 pts), payment integration (13 pts), RBAC (13 pts), multi-currency (13 pts), and thin QA/DevOps capacity risking rework or timeline slip.

Priority breakdown allocates the total estimate proportionally to story points within each priority band (Urgent, High, Medium, Low), scaled to the P50 total.</reasoning>

nonLabourLines.description: Stripe integration setup, sandbox/test transactions, and PCI-related tooling
Staging/cloud infrastructure (compute, storage, networking) for ~5-month build phase
Legacy Oracle data extraction tooling, temporary migration environment, and validation runs
Third-party services: transactional email provider, FX rate feed, search/full-text indexing service (setup + first months)
Contingency reserve for estimation uncertainty (no historical actuals available)

assumptions: No historical actuals (real spend data) are available for this project yet; all estimates are derived from backlog point sizing and role rate card only.

Assumed an average conversion of ~7 engineering hours per story point across roles, adjusted per task type (data migration and payment integration weighted higher; low-complexity items like decommissioning weighted lower).
Assumed a delivery window of approximately 22 weeks (5 months), used only to sanity-check that allocated hours stay within each role's FTE capacity, not as a hard deadline commitment.

QA Engineer (0.6 FTE) and DevOps Engineer (0.4 FTE) are staffed thinly relative to the backlog's compliance, payment-security, and infrastructure needs; this is flagged as a delivery risk rather than resolved by adding unbudgeted hours.
Backend Developer hours are the largest share of the budget due to RBAC, Stripe integration, legacy migration, audit logging, multi-currency settlement, and search all being backend-heavy.
Legacy data migration (PW-8) is assumed to require a dedicated one-off migration environment and validation tooling beyond standard staging infrastructure.
Non-labour costs are rough order-of-magnitude placeholders for third-party services and infrastructure; actual vendor quotes were not available.
Priority breakdown allocates the P50 total proportionally to story points within each priority band as a simplification; it does not imply strict phased delivery by priority alone.
Rate card figures and FTE availability are taken as given and used without markup or adjustment.

reductions.description: Descope Usage analytics and reporting (PW-19, Low, 8 pts) to a later phase; finance can use existing invoice exports in the interim.
reductions.effect: Removes an entire backlog item from this phase, reducing Frontend and Backend hours allocated to it.

reductions.description: Defer Admin back-office for support staff (PW-18, Low, 13 pts) until after launch; support staff can use direct DB/read-only tooling short-term.
reductions.effect: Removes a Low-priority item, freeing Backend and Frontend hours for higher-priority work or reducing total spend.

reductions.description: Reduce Accessibility pass (PW-15) scope to WCAG 2.2 AA on core customer journeys only (registration, dashboard, invoices, payments) rather than the full app, addressing remaining screens in a follow-up phase.
reductions.effect: Cuts Frontend and QA hours on the least-trafficked screens while keeping compliance risk on critical paths low.

reductions.description: Contract tests against helpdesk API (PW-23, Low, 5 pts) and Decommission legacy portal (PW-24, Low, 8 pts) can be pushed to a stabilization sprint after go-live rather than in the main build.
reductions.effect: Removes near-term DevOps and Backend hours; both tasks are safe to delay since they don't block core customer-facing launch.

reductions.description: Reduce Multi-currency support (PW-14) initial scope to USD + EUR only, adding PLN in a fast-follow release once daily FX feed integration is proven.
reductions.effect: Cuts Backend integration and QA test-matrix hours by roughly a third for this feature without blocking most customers.

reductions.description: Delay non-critical non-labour spend: third-party search/full-text indexing service setup, until Search feature (PW-13) is actually scheduled rather than provisioned upfront.
reductions.effect: Removes early non-labour spend commitment, pushed to when the feature enters development.
